To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in large multi agent systems the power law distribution is a necessary condition for agents to successfully go through other brokers to establish direct communication and that the power law is a consequence of the critical density of brokers in the market place.

the market share of agents in large multi-agent systems is governed by a power law distribution and that this power law distribution is the result of the interaction between the system and the agents.

the distribution of the market share among the information brokers is the power law and that this distribution is necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a critical density of agents in the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how agents can act as information brokers, and the conditions under which this will occur.
the emergence of power law distributions from agent interaction in a large distributed information market.
the conditions under which information markets are efficient, and the conditions under which they are not.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
agents that act as information broking agents in large distributed systems lower the cost of information only if the market shares among such brokers conform to a power-law distribution.
the power law and critical density are fundamental properties of large multi agent systems.
agents are not in charge of the system, but that the system is in charge of the agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
agents are able to establish direct communication in large distributed systems, provided the market shares of the information brokers conform to a power-law distribution.
the critical mass for information markets is determined by the distribution of market shares.
we have shown how the power law emerges in the market share distribution of agents that act as information broker in a simulated, large information marketplace.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power law and critical density of agents in large distributed systems are related.
the structure of a system determines the properties of the agents within the system.
, in large systems, agents can only be successful if they are willing to share information with other agents in order for the latter to become successful.
